[BRAND NAME] • [PRODUCT NAME] • [PRODUCT CATEGORY] • [PACKAGE TYPE] • [FLAVOR] • [HERO INGREDIENT] • [SUPPORTING INGREDIENTS] • [SERVING BOWL] • [PRODUCT BENEFITS] • [PRIMARY HEADLINE] • [SECONDARY LINE] • [BRAND COLORS] • [IMAGE RATIO]

Create a premium photorealistic FMCG advertisement for [PRODUCT NAME] by [BRAND NAME] in [IMAGE RATIO]. The result must resemble a high-budget commercial product campaign.

If a product image is provided, preserve the packaging exactly, including shape, colors, branding, typography, graphics, flavor, and label details. Do not redesign or alter any supplied elements. If no reference image is provided, generate an original [PACKAGE TYPE] for [PRODUCT CATEGORY].

If a background reference is provided, preserve its design language while creating an original adaptive abstract background automatically color-matched to the product's brand, flavor, and ingredients. Use premium organic shapes, embossed layers, subtle gradients, and textures. Avoid real environments and unnecessary props.

Position the package as the hero object (~50% of the composition) with [SERVING BOWL] slightly in front. Feature [HERO INGREDIENT] prominently and arrange [SUPPORTING INGREDIENTS] naturally around the bowl. Scatter a small amount of product naturally in the foreground.

Display "[PRIMARY HEADLINE]" and "[SECONDARY LINE]" only if provided, and show up to three [PRODUCT BENEFITS] using minimalist premium icons.

Use professional studio lighting, commercial product photography (50–70mm lens), moderate depth of field, authentic food textures, crisp highlights, natural shadows, and accurate typography.

Negative Prompt: No distorted packaging, altered branding, misspellings, duplicated ingredients, CGI, illustrations, floating objects, excessive props, blur, watermarks, cropped products, poor lighting, incorrect perspective, or competitor branding.

Deliver an ultra-high-resolution, social-media and print-ready premium advertising campaign in [4:5].

items.title: Kimi K3 cooked Opus 5, GPT-5.6, and Claude Fable 5 in my opinion.
items.summary:
Kimi K3 cooked Opus 5, GPT-5.6, and Claude Fable 5 in my opinion. 

Someone had Opus 5 generate this game from a single prompt.

Then gave GPT-5.6 Sol nothing but the gameplay video and asked it to recreate the experience.

The result was impressive.

GPT-5.6 Sol produced a fast, well-optimized prototype that captured much of the gameplay.

But Opus 5 still came out ahead in the areas that make a game feel believable: world composition, environmental detail, camera direction, atmosphere, and overall 3D scene coherence.

It’s becoming clear that raw code generation is only part of the story. Design judgment is starting to matter just as much.

items.title: There's a free trial running right now that gives you access to Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.6.
items.summary:
There's a free trial running right now that gives you access to Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.6.

GitLab added frontier models to their Duo Agent Platform. Their Ultimate free trial gives you full access.

Here's the setup:

→ Go to https://t.co/fgPXedrBDe and click "Start a free trial"

→ Sign in with Google or create an account

→ Fill out the trial form and create a project

→ Go to Settings → GitLab Duo → Configure features

→ Click the Duo Chat icon on the right toolbar

→ Pick your model and start using it

You get 30 days and 24 credits per user to run frontier models.

The catch: 24 credits means it's not unlimited. Use it for your most important work, not casual prompts. After 30 days you drop to GitLab Free.

But 30 days of free access to models most people are paying $20-200/month for? That's worth the 5 minutes of setup.

items.title: Moburst develops AI engine optimization capabilities for established companies - TechCrunch
items.summary: Mobile growth agency Moburst has built out a dedicated AI Engine Optimization practice aimed at established companies with existing app portfolios, betting that the category still lacks agencies with real depth rather than a rebranded service page. AI Engine Optimization, more commonly abbreviated AEO for Answer Engine Optimization, is the practice of structuring a brand’s content and web presence so AI systems such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google’s AI Overviews can confidently cite it when answering a user’s question directly, rather than showing a ranked list of links. For established companies vetting an AEO partner, the practical test is whether the agency can point to specific app-store-side work, not just web content changes, and whether it can describe a concrete process for reconciling inconsistent brand descriptions across many independent sources rather than treating that as someone else’s problem.

items.title: 1,100 AI workers sign letter asking US to support tools that 'pace the frontier of automated AI development' - Business Insider
items.summary: # Over 1,100 AI workers sign letter asking US to support tools that 'pace the frontier of automated AI development'. Senior officials at some of the nation's leading AI companies say it's time for the federal government to find a way to put the brakes on AI development if it's needed. "We request that the U.S. government support an international effort to develop the technical and governance tools needed to deliberately pace the frontier of automated AI development," reads an open letter signed by more than 1,100 AI workers from companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta. The letter zeroes in on "automated AI development," which refers to when AI will be capable of developing itself, something the industry calls "Recursive Self-Improvement." items.title: Another WTF moment.
items.summary:
Another WTF moment.

Hugging Face just open-sourced the fully local answer to OpenAI's Realtime voice API.

It's called speech-to-speech. You pip install it, run one command, and you get a WebSocket server at /v1/realtime that speaks the exact same protocol as OpenAI. Any client built for the OpenAI Realtime API can point at your machine instead and never know the difference.

This isn't a toy. The same pipeline runs in production as the conversation backend for thousands of Reachy Mini robots.

The stack is a four-stage cascade. Voice activity detection, speech to text, language model, text to speech. Each stage runs in its own thread with queues between them. Every stage is swappable via CLI flags.

Defaults out of the box are Silero VAD v5 for turn detection, NVIDIA's Parakeet TDT for transcription, and Qwen3-TTS for speech synthesis. The LLM slot points at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Hosted OpenAI, HF Inference Providers, OpenRouter, or a vLLM or llama.cpp server on your own hardware.

Swap components for your use case. Whisper, Faster Whisper, Lightning Whisper MLX, or Paraformer for STT. Kokoro-82M, Pocket TTS, ChatTTS, or MMS TTS for the voice. mlx-lm on Apple Silicon or Transformers on CUDA if you want the LLM in-process too.

Language coverage tracks whichever backends you pick. Parakeet TDT alone covers 25 European languages. Set --language auto and the STT auto-detects each spoken prompt and forwards it downstream. Set a specific code and the whole pipeline locks to that language.

Four run modes ship in the box. Realtime for the OpenAI-compatible WebSocket server. Local to talk through your machine's mic and speakers with no client at all. Raw WebSocket for a minimal custom client. Or a TCP socket mode where models run on a remote server and a thin client handles mic and playback.

The fully local recipe is two terminals. One runs llama.cpp serving Gemma 4. The other runs speech-to-speech pointed at that endpoint. No API keys. No network hops. No audio leaving the machine.

Apache 2.0 licensed. Python 3.10+. Docker compose file included. Sitting at 6.3k stars.

The thing worth understanding is what this really is. The Realtime API is becoming the default interface for voice agents. Hugging Face just released an open-source implementation of the server side that runs on your hardware, keeps your audio local, and lets you swap the model behind it every day if you want.

Every voice agent product being built right now assumes a paid API. This flips that assumption.

AI Engine Optimization, more commonly abbreviated AEO for Answer Engine Optimization, is the practice of structuring a brand’s content and web presence so AI systems such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google’s AI Overviews can confidently cite it when answering a user’s question directly, rather than showing a ranked list of links. items.title: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to unde
items.summary: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to understand what you're trying to achieve, but you're too lazy to type them. In these cases I like to lean back, switch to /voice and just ramble for like 10 minutes, total mess, anything goes, full stream of consciousness. Sometimes I declare it up top, something like "switching to speech recognition sorry for any typos...". Sometimes I turn it into a small interview of a few turns. But I find that the LLMs are somehow very good at reconstructing long incoherent rambles and often their echo of your own tangle of thoughts comes out quite a bit cleaner than what you started with. The result is that you improve the mind meld and have to correct things less from that point on.
